input.task: Search the catalogue for 'Meridian' and name the product you find.

provenance: kills the role tier for controls: every <button> becomes a <div> with its attributes and visible text intact, so no accessible name is computed for it and `{role: button, name: 'Search'}` finds nothing, while `{text: 'Search'}` still matches exactly what a human reads. Deliberately the SAME plan as l4-shop-duplicate-labels: the two cases differ only in the mutation, so the pair separates 'the name resolves to nothing' from 'the name resolves to two things' — one ends in element-not-found, the other in ambiguous-match, and both are rescued by the same text rung. The search flow rather than the sort flow is chosen on purpose: it is the flow the mutation's submit shim keeps alive, so a green here is also the evidence that the mutation breaks the agent and not the fixture (the ids-renamed lesson, mutation-catalog-integrity). Watched red by ablation (ADR-009): with `agent.MAX_FIXES = 0` the run stops at failure:locate, 'no tier resolved'. Live twin: quotes.toscrape.com renders its whole content as div/span and the observation contains none of it (live-quotes-js-role-tier-blind).
